title: Cold Chain Management
scope_note: Section 4 (Procedure) steps 4.1-4.12 of SOP-10, in DOH Warehouse Operations Manual, 2nd Edition 2022 (data/corpus/DOH_WOM-Manual.pdf, manual pages 174-183 = PDF pages 180-189). This SOP has no contingency section and no process flow diagram: it is a cold-chain overlay on the other SOPs, most of whose steps defer to another SOP or to the Cold Chain Logistics Management Manual of Operations - 5th Edition (2018). Order edges follow the warehouse lifecycle the SOP is organised by (preparation, receiving, put-away, storage, pick and pack, dispatch); the standing requirements 4.11 and 4.12 are roots. Manual numbering is irregular here (1.2 for 4.2, 1.1.2 for 4.7.2). Step text is the Key Step column verbatim, with long bulleted detail lists summarised to their lead line. Verified against the source document by the author on 2026-09-17; see data/graphs/VERIFICATION.md.

steps.text: Ensure compliance with guidelines and policies for health commodities that need to be handled through cold chain management

Estimating Storage Requirements for incoming deliveries of vaccines: it is important to know the size of these packages to properly estimate storage requirements before accepting vaccine deliveries; the volume per dose of each vaccine type may be found in the WHO Guidelines for International Packaging and Shipping of Vaccines
Estimating existing storage capacity for vaccines: to estimate existing storage capacity, cold rooms, freezer rooms and the cold chain equipment inventory must be updated and calculated
Inspection: conduct inspection routine for vaccines to ensure that specifications are met and that there are no damages prior to accepting the delivery

Receiving: as a general rule when receiving vaccine deliveries, always check for the presence of a temperature monitoring device and record the temperature reading upon opening of the box. If an electronic device is used, it has to be stopped and the temperature recorded in memory should be checked and verified for any temperature excursions that may potentially cause damage to the vaccines
Reject the vaccines and return them to the supplier or upper tier
steps.condition: vaccines are damaged either by heat or by freezing during transportation

steps.text: During Put away: please refer to Put away procedure (DOH-SCMS-WOM-SOP-03)
General Guidelines on Storage for Safe injection Equipment: please refer to Storage procedure (DOH-SCMS-WOM-SOP-04)

General Guidelines on Storage for Vaccines and Diluents: install standby generators to provide backup power in large vaccine stores; use appropriate cold rooms, freezer rooms, refrigerators, freezers, cold boxes and vaccine carriers for storage of EPI vaccines; choose an appropriate power source; conduct routine monitoring, recording and analysis of cold chain temperatures; set thermostat correctly based on manufacturer's instructions; replace old and broken door seal/gasket; arrange vaccines appropriately in the refrigerator; use vaccine baskets provided by the manufacturer; recognize damaged vaccines through Shake Test

Perform Temperature mapping exercise. This is essential in storage areas for health commodities with specific temperature-controlled requirements to ensure that vaccines are stored in accordance with its allowable temperature ranges

Temperature Monitoring: monitor the temperature inside the storage/transport equipment to ensure vaccine potency is maintained throughout the entire cold chain; it is recommended to use a Computerized Temperature Monitoring System which is directly linked with the temperature monitoring devices in different locations inside the cold room or freezer room for continuous monitoring
Proper placement of Temperature Monitoring Devices inside the Cold Room/Freezer Room, per the device rules for Walk-In Cold Room, Walk-In Freezer Room, and Cold Box & Vaccine Carriers
Inventory Management: please refer to Inventory Management Procedure in Storage and Warehousing (DOH-SCMS-WOM-SOP-04)

During Pick and Pack: please refer to Pick and Pack Procedure (DOH-SCMS-WOM-SOP-05). Use correct cold boxes and vaccine carriers for vaccine transport; prepare sufficient number of conditioned ice packs in packing freeze-sensitive vaccines and provide extra frozen ice packs for use in case of delay; use WHO/UNICEF PQS compliant vaccine carrier; arrange ice packs and vaccines inside the vaccine carrier properly; place a thermometer or freeze indicator on top of mixed vaccines or freeze-sensitive vaccines as necessary

During Dispatch: coordinate with 3PL and/or in-house transport services for the schedule of shipment; ensure to use appropriate refrigerated vehicles for transporting vaccines; notify recipient on the estimated day/time of arrival to their warehouse/facility; countercheck the documents, quantity, and actual item during dispatch process ensuring that relevant documents are stamped as received by the 3PL; consolidate, countercheck, and maintain carbon copies of Relevant Documents for filing and review of Supply Officer as necessary

Preventive Maintenance of Cold Chain Equipment: all storekeepers, health workers and staff in charge of a vaccine storage facility should be able to perform preventive maintenance routinely to keep their respective cold chain equipment in optimal working condition; determine needed budget to ensure complete and functional cold chain infrastructure and equipment

Contingency Plan: specific actions and contingency plans should be clearly laid out, disseminated, understood, and followed. Key elements: ensuring that all affected vaccines are stored within the recommended storage temperature of +2 to +8 degrees Celsius as soon as possible; identifying alternative locations where vaccines can be safely stored or where ice can be obtained at short notice; preparing and maintaining at least two emergency response plans; posting emergency contact details of key personnel; clearly describing initial and follow-up actions inside and outside of working hours; reviewing and rehearsing the procedures in the plan at least once a year
